look_here_first: Check the thick, often somewhat fleshy narrow alternate leaves and the long terminal cluster of small yellow heads, often borne predominantly on one side of branches. Coastal wet-saline habitat is a supporting cue, not proof by itself.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: Rhizomatous perennial goldenrod of coastal marshes, dunes, and brackish margins.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: Leaves alternate, comparatively thick and narrow; inspect leaf texture and venation rather than flower color.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: Numerous small yellow composite heads in a terminal, often one-sided inflorescence.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: Inflorescence architecture and fleshy leaf texture together are more useful than plant height.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: Check mature involucres and foliage against closely related seaside goldenrods before final ID.
